name: Climber Antagonist & Push (In-Season)
description: The non-negotiable weekly push routine for anyone who climbs 2+ times a week. Balances the chronic pull-dominance of climbing.
ideal_schedule: morning before climbing day or full rest day
notes: Keep RPE 6-7 in-season; save the last rep in the tank.

name: Climbing Finger Strength Protocol (Repeaters)
description: Dedicated hangboard finger-strength block using the 7/3 repeater protocol plus prehab.
ideal_schedule: after a full warm-up, before climbing or as a standalone
notes: Must be fully warmed up. Stop the session at the first sign of pulley discomfort.

name: Climber Off-Season Strength Foundation
description: Three-day off-season block: lower-body strength, upper-body strength, and antagonist/conditioning. Builds a deep well for the climbing season.
notes: Keep climbing volume low during this block — strength gains need recovery budget.

name: Pre-Climb Warm-Up (15 min)
description: Targeted 15-minute warm-up to prep fingers, shoulders, and spine for climbing.
notes: Warm up the weakest link first: fingers and shoulders.

name: Climber Shoulder Prehab (3x/week)
description: Short, daily-ish shoulder prehab for high-volume climbers. Ten minutes of insurance.
notes: Prioritize consistency over intensity — 10 minutes three times a week beats 45 once a week.

name: Climbing Travel Workout (Bodyweight, 20 min)
description: Maintains antagonist and foundation work with zero equipment — perfect for travel.
notes: If travel is over a week, rotate in hangboard work on a portable board where possible.

name: Climber Pre-Season Power Block
description: Pre-season power primer for sport and competition climbers. Campusing, explosive pulls, core integration.
ideal_schedule: early in the week, at least 48h from heavy climbing
notes: Advanced only. 40+ climbers scale back campusing.

name: Climber Elbow Prehab (Medial + Lateral)
description: Forearm balance routine — reverse wrist curls, finger extensors, soft-tissue. Directly addresses "climber's elbow".
ideal_schedule: pair with antagonist work or as a stand-alone
notes: If elbow pain is acute, reduce load and switch to rehab protocol.

name: Cyclist Off-Season Strength Foundation
description: Three-day off-season strength block for cyclists: glute/hamstring focus, unilateral leg work, core.
notes: Reduce cycling volume during the heaviest strength weeks.

name: Cyclist Glute + Hamstring Prehab
description: Short prehab routine addressing the posterior-chain weakness + hip flexor tightness that cyclists chronically develop.

name: Cyclist In-Season Maintenance
description: Twice-weekly maintenance block during the cycling season. Low volume, high-priority prehab.
ideal_schedule: rest day or morning before evening ride
notes: Keep RPE 6-7; save legs for the bike.

name: MTB Upper-Body + Grip
description: MTB-specific upper-body work — forearm endurance, pulling strength, core anti-rotation for descents.

name: Runner Off-Season Strength
description: Three-day off-season strength block for runners: posterior chain, calves, unilateral, core.
notes: Reduce running volume during heavy strength weeks.

name: Runner Prehab (Knee + Ankle + Glute)
description: Daily-ish prehab addressing the top runner injuries: PFPS, IT band, Achilles, shin splints.

name: Pre-Run Warm-up Drills
description: Dynamic warm-up with running-specific drills — A-skip, leg swings, activation.

name: Runner In-Season Strength Maintenance
description: Twice-weekly in-season strength — just enough to hold gains without stealing from running.

name: Achilles / Calf Rehab Protocol
description: Alfredson-style eccentric protocol for Achilles tendinopathy, plus calf foundations.
notes: See a PT for individualized programming. Protocol based on Alfredson et al.

name: BJJ Neck + Shoulder Prehab
description: Short prehab addressing the shoulder pulls, neck strain, and elbow issues that stack up in grapplers.

name: Pre-Roll Warm-up
description: Grappling-specific warm-up: shrimping, hip mobility, shoulder prep.

name: Grappler Grip + Core
description: Grip-endurance and anti-rotation core — supplementary block for gi/no-gi balance.

name: BJJ In-Season Maintenance
description: Twice-weekly in-season strength — stays out of the way of mat training.

name: Golfer Rotational Power
description: Rotational-power block for developing club-head speed with sound mechanics.

name: Pre-Round Mobility
description: 15-minute mobility flow priming T-spine rotation, hips, shoulders before a round.
notes: Avoid heavy static stretching that stiffens the thoracic spine.

name: Golfer Elbow + Shoulder Prehab
description: Specific prehab for lead-shoulder impingement and medial/lateral epicondylitis.

name: Golfer Off-Season Strength
description: Golf-specific off-season block: glutes, core, unilateral, rotational.

name: Senior Golf Joint Health
description: Age-friendly maintenance routine emphasizing joint mobility, balance, and gentle strength for 55+ golfers.
notes: 50+/60+ athletes — reduce intensity if any joint symptom flares.

name: Tennis Off-Season Strength
description: Off-season block for tennis: unilateral leg, rotational core, shoulder strength + prehab.

name: Tennis Shoulder + Elbow Prehab
description: Overhead-athlete prehab targeting rotator cuff, scap control, and medial/lateral elbow.

name: Tennis In-Season Maintenance
description: Twice-weekly in-season strength maintenance — low volume, prehab-dominant.

name: Rotational + Unilateral Power
description: Rotational power block transferable across racquet sports, golf, baseball.

name: Pre-Season Ski Prep Block
description: Pre-season ski prep: eccentric quad, lateral power, single-leg strength. The staple 6-8 week block before ski season.
notes: Start 8 weeks before ski season. Ramp volume; taper last week.

name: Skier Knee Prehab
description: Targeted prehab for ACL/MCL resilience: VMO, glute med, terminal knee extension, balance.

name: Pre-Ski-Day Warm-up
description: In-car or mountain-lodge warm-up to avoid cold-start ski injuries.

name: Ski-Specific Eccentric Strength
description: Focused eccentric strength day for advanced skiers preparing for steeps and moguls.

name: Snowboard Shoulder + Wrist Prehab
description: Snowboard-specific prehab — addresses FOOSH-wrist risk and shoulder health.

name: General Athletic Foundation (Off-Season)
description: Three-day off-season foundation for any hybrid athlete: squat, hinge, push, pull, carry, core.
notes: Works for cyclists, runners, climbers, grapplers, racquet players between seasons.

name: 40+ Athlete Joint Health
description: Age-friendly maintenance: mobility, controlled strength, balance. Daily-ish for athletes 40+.
notes: 40+/50+/60+ athletes. Skip anything that flares joint pain.

name: Travel Bodyweight Workout
description: Zero-equipment full-body session for any sport — maintains antagonist balance while traveling.

name: Desk Worker Daily Mobility
description: Daily 10-minute desk-break routine addressing T-spine, hips, wrists, shoulders.
notes: Treat like brushing teeth — daily.

name: Swimmer Off-Season Strength
description: Three-day off-season block for swimmers: pulling strength, posterior shoulder, core.

name: Swimmer Shoulder Prehab
description: Daily-ish shoulder routine specifically targeting the posterior capsule + rotator-cuff balance issues swimmers accumulate.

name: Pre-Swim Warmup (Dryland)
description: 10-minute dryland warmup before pool entry — shoulder, T-spine, core activation.

name: CrossFit Skill Work — Olympic Lift Fundamentals
description: Technical skill session for power clean / snatch progressions. Light loads, high reps per set.
notes: Skill sessions should not be conditioning sessions. Keep heart rate moderate.

name: CrossFit Posterior Chain Day
description: Deadlift-focused strength session for CrossFitters — addresses common posterior-chain neglect.

name: Soccer Off-Season Strength
description: Three-day off-season block for soccer players: unilateral leg, ACL prehab, core.

name: ACL Prehab Protocol
description: Evidence-based ACL injury prevention for soccer, basketball, volleyball, skiing — glute med, landing mechanics, hamstring.
notes: Based on PEP / FIFA 11+ components.

name: Pre-Game Warmup (FIFA 11+ style)
description: 15-minute dynamic warmup combining running drills, strength, and plyometric components.

name: Basketball Jumper Prehab
description: Jumper's knee / Achilles prehab + lateral movement work for basketball, volleyball.

name: Team Sport In-Season Maintenance
description: Twice-weekly in-season maintenance for field/court athletes — low CNS load, prehab-dominant.

name: Pack Prep Strength Block
description: Pre-trip strength block for loaded hiking / backcountry — step-ups, carries, eccentric descent.
notes: Start 8 weeks before a big trip. Progress pack weight gradually.

name: Hiker Descent Prep
description: Eccentric quad and knee prehab for long descents. Essential for anyone doing mountain trails.
notes: Eccentric loading is hard; ease into it.

name: Ruck + Mobility Combo
description: 45-minute rucking session bookended with 10 min mobility each end. Zone-2 training + carry prep.

name: Post-Hike Recovery
description: Calves, quads, lower back recovery after a long hike or multi-day trip.

name: BJJ Supplemental Strength (In-Season, 2x/wk)
description: In-season strength maintenance for BJJ practitioners. Mixes direct_strength with antagonist push to balance the chronic pull/flex dominance of grappling.
ideal_schedule: morning of light-roll days or full rest days
notes: Keep RPE 6-7 in-season. Drop a set if sessions the next day feel heavier than usual.

name: Boxer Shoulder Prehab & Neck (3x/week)
description: Daily-ish shoulder + neck insurance for boxers. Twenty minutes rotator cuff + cervical resilience before sparring days.
notes: Boxers chronically overuse anterior shoulder and under-train neck. Do not skip even in heavy training weeks.

name: Wrestler Hip/Grip Power (Off-Season, 2x/wk)
description: Off-season explosive hip and grip strength for wrestlers and MMA athletes. Heavy hinge, loaded carries, neck work.
notes: Keep conditioning light on these days — this block is CNS-heavy.

name: Striker Antagonist Push/Pull Balance (2x/wk)
description: Scapular retraction, posterior chain, and pull-dominant work to offset the chronic anterior-shoulder overuse of boxing, kickboxing, and muay thai.
ideal_schedule: morning before training or rest day
notes: The more you hit bags, the more this matters. Ten minutes of face pulls will outlast any YouTube abs routine.

name: Martial Artist Travel Workout (Bodyweight, 20 min)
description: Maintains antagonist and prehab with zero equipment — perfect for travel, competitions, or a hotel seminar weekend.
ideal_schedule: hotel room or any open space
notes: Rotate in shadow-boxing rounds if you want added conditioning.

name: Squash Conditioning Circuit
description: Glycolytic-focused court-burst conditioning circuit to match the energy system demand of hard squash rallies.
ideal_schedule: 2-3 days before hard matches, not same day
notes: Squash has higher glycolytic demand than any other racquet sport. This circuit mimics that.

name: Racquet Pre-Match Warm-Up
description: Sport-agnostic 15-minute warm-up for any racquet player: dynamic shoulder, hip, wrist, plus racquet-swing-specific rotational prep.
notes: Ramp pace through the warm-up; end with 2-3 light rotational swings.

name: Racquet Off-Season Rotational Power
description: Off-season power block: med-ball throws, rotational presses, single-leg plyos. Builds the torque foundation for in-season stroke velocity.
notes: Keep total volume moderate — power requires quality, not grinding.

name: Over-50 Pickleballer Joint Health
description: Joint-friendly 3x/week strength and prehab routine designed for the 50+ pickleballer. Bulletproofs knees, ankles, wrists, and shoulders.
notes: Consistency over intensity. The routine is designed to feel sustainable forever.

name: Travel Racquet Workout (Bodyweight)
description: Equipment-free 20-minute routine for the traveling racquet player. Holds onto strength, mobility, and shoulder balance.
notes: Bring a light band if possible — it dramatically expands the menu.

name: Paddler's Upper-Body Endurance (2x/week)
description: The weekly pulling endurance routine for paddlers — cable paddle pulls, landmine rotation, shoulder prehab.
ideal_schedule: non-consecutive days, morning before evening paddle OK
notes: Keep RPE 7. Paddle pulls and rotations are primary — prehab is non-negotiable.

name: Surfer Pop-Up Power & Shoulder (Pre-Season, 2x/week)
description: Pre-season block building the pop-up pattern, quad/glute drive, and shoulder endurance for a long surf trip.
notes: Build the pop-up and lower-body power in the weeks before your trip.

name: Pre-Session Warm-Up for Paddlers (10 min)
description: 10-minute mobility + activation warm-up for paddlers before water time.
notes: Prioritize shoulders, t-spine, and hips — the three things paddling punishes most.

name: Wakeboard / Kite Off-Season Strength (3x/week)
description: Off-season strength block for wakeboarders, kitesurfers, and wing-foilers. Heavy legs, core, and grip.
notes: Focus on unilateral strength and balance — wake and kite demand single-leg and foot-to-foot power.

name: Traveling Surfer Workout (Bodyweight, 20 min)
description: Zero-equipment surfer maintenance routine — perfect for trips.
notes: Keeps the pop-up pattern primed plus shoulder endurance and core.

name: Over-50 Paddler Joint Health (3x/week)
description: Joint-friendly prehab + strength routine for paddlers 50+. Emphasizes mobility and connective-tissue work.
ideal_schedule: morning, not paired with paddle day
notes: Older paddlers need more mobility and less max strength. Keep reps 10-15, load moderate.

name: Dragon Boat Rotational Power (2x/week)
description: Rotational power block for dragon boat paddlers — landmine rotation, medball slams, paddle erg sprints.
notes: Keep CNS load visible — rotational max should not stack with heavy pulling.

name: Competitive Rower Erg + Strength (3x/week)
description: Competitive rower in-season block — ergs, pulling, posterior chain, shoulder prehab.
notes: Scale the erg intervals and strength load independently — both have high CNS cost.

name: Soccer ACL + Adductor Prehab Protocol
description: Full prehab stack for soccer's two top injury sites — non-contact ACL and adductor strains. Combines TKE, Copenhagen, single-leg mechanics, and deceleration.
ideal_schedule: warmup before lower-body day or as stand-alone
notes: Keep RPE 5-7. Miss this before you miss heavy squats.

name: Soccer Eccentric Hamstring Progression (Nordic)
description: The non-negotiable hamstring-strain prevention protocol for anyone running and cutting 2+ times per week. Band-assisted Nordic progressing to full Nordic.
notes: Start where you can control the eccentric — ego out of it. Stop if hamstring cramps or sharp pain.

name: Basketball Vertical Jump Development
description: Off-season vertical-jump block — stepped plyo progression from drop-stick to depth jump, with strength-based foundation support.
ideal_schedule: off-season, separated from heavy lower-body work by 48h
notes: Advanced plyos only with 12+ weeks of strength foundation behind them. 40+ athletes scale volume down 40%.

name: Basketball Ankle + Knee Prehab
description: Combined ankle + knee prehab for the two most common basketball injuries: lateral ankle sprain and patellar tendinopathy.
notes: Consistency > intensity. Three times a week for 20 min beats 60 min once.

name: Volleyball Shoulder Complex Prehab
description: Rotator cuff + lower trap + thoracic mobility block for spikers and setters. Addresses the cumulative overhead shoulder load of a volleyball season.
notes: Every exercise here is low-CNS — do not skip on tired days.

name: Baseball Rotational Power
description: Pre-season rotational power block for hitters and pitchers — cable lifts, scoop throws, and anti-rotation core.
notes: Rotational power is high-CNS. Schedule far from competition.

name: Rugby Neck Strength + Tackle Prep
description: Contact-sport neck strengthening + posterior-chain power. Reduces concussion risk and preps the body for tackles.
notes: Neck iso work is sub-max always. Progress slowly.

name: Over-40 Rec Soccer Joint Health
description: Joint-friendly maintenance block for adult rec players over 40. Emphasizes mobility, glute med, and eccentric hamstring at sub-max load.
notes: No max plyos. No 5x5 squats. This is the long game.

name: Pre-Game Warm-Up — Soccer
description: 15-minute dynamic warmup for soccer — FIFA 11+ style blended with deceleration and TKE activation.
notes: Skip the static stretching. Move progressively from easy mobility to sprinting.

name: Pre-Game Warm-Up — Basketball
description: 15-minute dynamic warmup for basketball — ankle CARs, glute activation, and progressive jumping.
notes: Spend the most time on ankles and knees — the two tissues most likely to fail.

name: Team Sport Off-Season Foundation
description: 3x/week off-season foundation — front squat, trap bar, upper-body push/pull, core. Builds the chassis for the competitive season.
notes: Progress load week over week. Track your main lifts.

name: Travel Team-Sport Bodyweight Workout
description: 20-minute bodyweight maintenance workout — perfect for travel weeks, tournaments, or road trips.
notes: Maintain the movements. Strength is use-it-or-lose-it over long travel.

name: Lacrosse / Hockey Shoulder + Core
description: Off-field combined shoulder prehab + rotational core block for stick-sport athletes.
notes: Shoulder health is the limiting factor long-term. Build the insurance.

name: Yogi Hamstring Strength (Often Neglected)
description: Strength for the hamstrings — the one thing most yogis miss in all their forward folding.
notes: Flexibility without strength is a route to SI-joint pain. Do not skip.

name: Pilates Supplemental Strength
description: Compound-strength supplement for Pilates-focused athletes who want to build load capacity.
notes: Pilates alone underloads the posterior chain — this fills that gap.

name: Calisthenics Pull Progression
description: Progressive pull routine — scap → body row → pull-up → muscle-up pathway.
notes: Skill + strength — respect fatigue, avoid max-effort back-to-back days.

name: Calisthenics Pushing Progression (Planche / Handstand)
description: Pressing skill progression — planche lean, handstand, ring dips, chaturanga.
notes: Holds first, reps second. Protect wrists with thorough warm-up.

name: Parkour Landing & Ankle Prep
description: Ankle, foot, and landing-mechanic routine specifically for parkour athletes.
notes: Ankles and wrists do 90% of parkour damage — train them accordingly.

name: Inline Skater Lateral Power
description: Lateral hip power and slide-board work for inline and speed skaters.
notes: Lateral plyos are high-CNS — keep spacing.

name: Roller Derby Off-Season Strength
description: Full off-season strength block for roller derby athletes: squat, hinge, lateral power.
notes: Contact + lateral skating = most demanding skating sport. Build deep reserves.

name: Hip-Hop Dancer Explosive Power
description: Explosive lower-body power for hip-hop dancers — freezes, power moves, battles.
notes: Reserve for off-competition weeks; high CNS demand.

name: Dance Pre-Rehearsal Warm-Up
description: Universal 15-minute dance warm-up hitting feet, hips, spine, and shoulders.
notes: Do not skip the feet — calves and intrinsic foot need heat first.

name: Over-50 Yoga Practitioner Strength
description: Joint-friendly strength block for older yoga practitioners — preserves bone and muscle.
notes: Emphasize controlled tempo and full ROM over heavy load.

name: Travel Calisthenics Workout (Bodyweight, 30 min)
description: Bodyweight-only strength session for hotel rooms and travel — full-body coverage.
notes: Hit push, pull (if bar/rings available), legs, and core in one pass.

name: Powerlifter Accessory & Prehab
description: Accessory and joint-health work that supports the big three. Wrist, T-spine, elbow, and hip resilience for athletes doing heavy SBD training.
notes: Heavy only on main lifts — keep accessories at RPE 7 or below.

name: CrossFit Shoulder & Wrist Prehab
description: Prehab insurance for high-volume CrossFitters. Rotator cuff, scapular stability, and wrist mobility to survive the mixed-modal load.
notes: Thirty minutes three times a week beats two hours once a week.

name: Strongman Event Prep, Pre-Season
description: Pre-season event-specific block: yoke, sandbag, stone, heavy carries. Build the engine for competition day.
notes: Rotate event rotation weekly — yoke one week, stones the next — to manage CNS.

name: Kettlebell Sport Grip & Shoulder Endurance
description: Competition-pattern clean-and-jerk volume plus grip endurance work. Specific to long-set kettlebell sport.
notes: Manage grip carefully — forearm fatigue ruins technique before shoulders do.

name: Bodybuilder Injury Prevention Accessory
description: Joint-health work that most hypertrophy programs skip. Rotator cuff, elbow prehab, T-spine, hip mobility.
notes: Treat it as a training session — structured, not casual.

name: Rider Core & Hip Asymmetry Correction
description: Corrects the postural drift riding creates. Core, hip opener, T-spine rotation, and asymmetry work.
ideal_schedule: on non-riding days or morning of light rides
notes: Rein-hand dominance builds asymmetry week by week — this is the counter.

name: Endurance Rider Glute & Adductor Circuit
description: Adductor, glute, and core endurance for multi-hour saddle work. Isometric-heavy circuit.
notes: The goal is endurance at the saddle position — not max strength.

name: Polo Rotational Power, Pre-Season
description: Explosive rotational work matching the polo mallet swing. Core, obliques, single-arm strength.
notes: Rotation is mallet-side dominant; give extra volume on the non-dominant side.

name: Paraglider Landing Prep & Neck
description: Landing-absorption mechanics + four-way neck work. Insurance against the two highest-risk moments in the sport.
notes: Neck conditioning is a sustained game — progress by 10s per week, not by load.

name: Over-50 Strength Athlete Joint Health
description: Joint-friendly accessory and mobility work for 50+ strength athletes. Protects shoulders, hips, spine.
notes: Load stays moderate; ROM and consistency matter more than weight.

name: Pre-Training Warm-Up (Strength Sports)
description: Universal 10-minute warm-up for strength sports. T-spine, wrists, hips, shoulders — the usual suspects.
notes: Do this before every training day — skip at your own risk.

name: Equestrian Pre-Ride Activation
description: Ten-minute pre-ride activation targeting riders' tightest spots: hip flexors, T-spine, adductors.
notes: Ten minutes, every ride. Your horse appreciates the improved seat.

name: Splitboard Pre-Season Strength A: Squat, Eccentric, Rotation
description: Bilateral squat strength, then eccentric single-leg control for the descent, then anti-rotation and rotation for the turn. Built from the demands of the sport: quad-dominant eccentric load, knee stability, trunk rotation under load.
notes: Bilateral squat strength, then eccentric single-leg control for the descent, then anti-rotation and rotation for the turn. Built from the demands of the sport: quad-dominant eccentric load, knee stability, trunk rotation under load.

name: Splitboard Pre-Season Strength B: Hinge, Power, Upper
description: Hip hinge strength, a short power block, then the pressing and pulling a full day of touring and carrying asks for. Complements Strength A.
notes: Hip hinge strength, a short power block, then the pressing and pulling a full day of touring and carrying asks for. Complements Strength A.

name: Splitboard In-Season Maintenance
description: The minimum that keeps strength on the board through the season: one squat, one loaded step for the skin track, one pull, calves, trunk. Two sets where three would cost the next tour.
notes: The minimum that keeps strength on the board through the season: one squat, one loaded step for the skin track, one pull, calves, trunk. Two sets where three would cost the next tour.

name: Easy Strength — 5-Lift Base
description: Autoregulated — never miss a rep, never grind, leave 1-2 in the tank, finish feeling stronger than you started. ~60-80% of max on the 2x5s (Dan John / Pavel, Easy Strength). When the weight feels light, add load.

name: MTB Pre-Season Strength: Leg Endurance and Trunk
description: Repeated-effort leg strength for long climbs, paired with the anti-rotation trunk work that holds the bike straight when the legs are tired. Circuit format, steady pace, short rest.
notes: Repeated-effort leg strength for long climbs, paired with the anti-rotation trunk work that holds the bike straight when the legs are tired. Circuit format, steady pace, short rest.

name: MTB Pre-Season Strength: Power and Hinge
description: Power for the punchy climbs and the hip hinge that unloads the front of the bike, with unilateral squat endurance and trunk work between. Circuit format.
